introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Duration: three and a quarter hours.**

Answer FOUR questions in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing at least ONE question from SECTION B and TWO from SECTION C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each.

Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references.

Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed.

Materials required: Topographic map, graph paper and two outline maps of Cameroon.

Answer question ONE and three others, choosing at least ONE question from SECTION B and TWO from SECTION C ». `regles_choix` porte le minimum par section (B : 1 parmi 2 ; C : 2 parmi 4) ; la question 1 (Section A, obligatoire) n'a pas de règle ; la règle « 4 questions en tout » n'est pas exprimable en entier et est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`. Les questions 2 et 3 sont rangées en SECTION B (l'en-tête « FIELD WORK AND TECHNIQUES » précède la question 2 et la question 3 suit sans nouvel en-tête) ; les questions 4 à 7 en SECTION C (« CAMEROON »).

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées de mémoire, sans accès à une source. Les faits cités (régions, institutions, sites) sont ceux de la géographie du Cameroun couramment enseignée ; les chiffres sont arrondis et donnés avec « about » quand ils ne sont pas certains ; aucune statistique précise n'est avancée. À relire par un géographe avant mise en avant.

Question 2 : le sujet demande de s'appuyer sur le travail de terrain PERSONNEL du candidat ; il n'existe donc pas de réponse unique. Le corrigé est un modèle de méthode, illustré par le thème (i) (variation d'une caractéristique du sol le long d'une pente) ; les résultats chiffrés ou qualitatifs cités sont des résultats typiques annoncés comme tels, pas des données réelles. L'élève doit remplacer l'exemple par sa propre enquête.

Question 2 : le sujet imprime « (5 marks) » une seule fois pour l'ensemble b) (i) et (ii) ; le bloc b) est donc codé à 5 points (et non 5 + 5). Les points imprimés somment à 23 (5 + 5 + 6 + 2 + 3 + 2), conformément à la page de garde.

questions.enonce_markdown: a) With the aid of a sketch map, describe the area where the fieldwork was carried out. (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model answer, illustrated with topic (i): variation in soil characteristics (for example soil depth, moisture and texture) down a slope. Replace the example by your own fieldwork.**

**Sketch map (about 2 marks).** Draw a labelled sketch map with a title, a north arrow, a scale (or "not to scale"), a key and a frame. Show: the slope (contour lines or a hill-shaped sign), the line of the transect from the top (crest) to the foot of the slope, the sampling sites numbered 1 to 8 (for example every 10 m), the stream or valley floor, the footpath or road, the farms or plots, the vegetation (forest edge, grass, crops) and the nearest village.

**Description (about 3 marks).**

- **Location**: the village or locality, the Division and Region, the distance and direction from a known town or the school.
- **Relief and drainage**: a hillslope about 100 m long, convex at the top, straight in the middle and concave at the foot, falling towards a small stream; the gradient (for example from about 15 degrees at the top to a few degrees at the foot, measured with a clinometer).
- **Soil and rock**: the parent rock, the main soil colour at the top and at the foot.
- **Vegetation and land use**: grass and shrubs on the upper slope, food crops (cassava, maize, cocoyam) in the middle, a raffia or swampy fringe at the foot; footpaths and houses.
- **Climate**: the tropical climate of the area, with a rainy and a dry season, and the date and season of the fieldwork.

*Marks: sketch map 2 (title, north, scale, key, features); description of the area 3.*

questions.enonce_markdown:
b) (i) What was the purpose of the investigations?

(ii) State the type of data that was required. (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(b)(i) Purpose (aim and hypotheses).** To find out how selected soil characteristics (depth, moisture, texture, pH, organic matter) vary from the top to the foot of the slope, and to explain the variation. A hypothesis can be stated: "Soil depth and moisture increase down the slope" (the null hypothesis: there is no change). Secondary aims: to find the best land use for each part of the slope and to practise geographical skills.

**(b)(ii) Type of data required.**

- **Primary data (collected in the field)**: *quantitative* (soil depth in cm, slope angle in degrees, soil moisture in per cent, soil pH value, percentage of sand, silt and clay, number of plant species) and *qualitative* (soil colour compared with a colour chart, structure, texture by feel, description of vegetation cover and land use).
- **Secondary data (from other sources)**: topographic map of the area for the slope and location, rainfall records of the nearest meteorological station, soil map or agricultural office reports.

*Marks: purpose 2 to 3; types of data 2 to 3.*

questions.enonce_markdown: c) How was the data collected, processed, and presented? (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Collection (2 marks).**

- A **transect** (systematic line sampling) was laid from the crest to the foot of the slope with a tape and ranging poles; a sampling point was fixed every 10 m, with three samples at each point to reduce error.
- Instruments: a soil auger or spade (depth, samples), a clinometer or abney level (slope angle), a pH test kit or meter, a moisture meter or the weighing of samples before and after oven drying, sample bags and labels, a colour chart, a notebook and a field sheet.
- Observations were recorded on a field data sheet at each point; a questionnaire or interviews with farmers on land use were used where necessary.

**Processing (2 marks).** The data were checked and tabulated; averages of the three samples at each site were calculated; moisture content was worked out as (wet mass minus dry mass) divided by wet mass, as a percentage; texture was classified using the soil texture triangle; slope angles were classified; a correlation (for example Spearman's rank correlation between distance down the slope and soil moisture) was used to test the strength of the relation.

**Presentation (2 marks).** Tables of results; line graphs or bar charts of depth, moisture and pH against distance down the slope; a labelled cross-section (transect profile) of the slope with the soil profile at each site; a scatter graph with a best-fit line; photographs and annotated sketches; a map showing the sampling sites.

*Marks: collection 2; processing 2; presentation 2.*

questions.enonce_markdown: d) What was the conclusion arrived at after processing the data? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Conclusion (typical result for the example; the candidate must give the results of his or her own study).** The soil changed regularly down the slope: it was thin, stony, dry and coarse (sandy) at the top, and thicker, darker, wetter, finer-textured (more clay and silt) and richer in organic matter at the foot. The hypothesis was therefore accepted: soil depth and moisture increased down the slope, and the correlation was strong and positive. (Mention any anomaly, for example a farmed plot in the middle of the slope.)

*Marks: a clear statement of the result 1; whether the hypothesis was accepted or rejected 1.*

questions.enonce_markdown: e) What possibly accounts for the results obtained? (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Explanation (3 marks; any three developed points).**

- **Gravity and water movement.** Rain splash, slope wash and soil creep carry fine soil particles, nutrients and humus from the steep upper slope to the gentle lower slope, where they are deposited; the top therefore loses material (thin soil) and the foot gains it (thick soil).
- **Leaching and drainage.** Water drains downslope by throughflow, so the foot has a higher water table and is wetter, while the crest is freely drained and dry.
- **Vegetation and organic matter.** More vegetation and more leaf litter at the foot give more humus, darker soil and a better structure; the decomposition is faster in the moist conditions.
- **Human activity.** Cultivation and grazing on the middle slope expose the soil and increase erosion; the deposition at the foot is increased by it.

*Marks: 1 per developed point.*

questions.enonce_markdown: f) State the significance of the fieldwork. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Significance (2 marks).** The study showed which part of the slope is best for which crop, and where erosion is most serious, so it helps farmers to use the land properly (for example food crops at the foot, trees or grass on the crest) and to apply soil conservation (terracing, contour ploughing, mulching). It also gave candidates first-hand experience of geographical enquiry: observation, measurement, data processing and the testing of a hypothesis, and it provides data that planners and the agricultural service can use.

*Marks: any two points (1 each).*
